{"consolidated_memory":"**Duplicate Charge Issues in billing/webhooks/stripe.py—Four Separate Incidents**

This is a recurring problem in the Stripe webhook consumer that has manifested four times with different root causes and fixes. All incidents shared the same signal: two ledger rows sharing one event id, and all were reproducible by redelivering the same webhook id twice.

**Incident 1: Schema Drift [2026-01-13]**
- File: billing/webhooks/stripe.py
- Trigger: appeared only after client had already retried once
- Root cause: schema drift between migration and model
- Fix: regenerated model from migration and pinned checksum (PR #2145, branch fix/duplicate-charge-1)
- Result: memory settled at 933 MB instead of climbing past 5 GB

**Incident 2: Floating Point Rounding [2026-01-30]**
- File: billing/webhooks/stripe.py
- Trigger: turned up only after rolling restart of fleet
- Root cause: floating point rounding in money path
- Fix: moved arithmetic to integer minor units (PR #4042, branch fix/duplicate-charge-2)
- Result: p99 latency fell from 5.4 s to 905 ms

**Incident 3: Connection Pool Exhaustion [2026-02-17]**
- File: billing/webhooks/stripe.py
- Trigger: appeared only for payloads above roughly 2 megabytes
- Root cause: connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Fix: raised pool ceiling and put bounded wait queue in front of it (PR #8897, branch fix/duplicate-charge-3)
- Result: flaky test went from 2 failures per 100 runs to zero

**Incident 4: Missing Composite Index [2026-07-06]**
- File: billing/webhooks/stripe.py
- Trigger: appeared only for records carrying non-ASCII names
- Root cause: missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at)
- Fix: added composite index and backfilled in batches (PR #9185, branch fix/duplicate-charge-4)
- Stack: Python
- Covering test: tests/billing/test_stripe_webhook.py
- Result: throughput rose 35%, to 112 requests per second"}
